source.title: Do Foundation Models Know Geometry? Probing Frozen Features for Continuous Physical Measurement

record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures representational similarity between diverse encoders and argues that similar geometric-probe accuracy does not require representational convergence. It refines the convergence claim, but does not test a scale-dependent rise in alignment.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many probe-accuracy results, but those measure how well geometry can be read out, not representational alignment itself. They are recorded under fits_no_version. The CKA comparisons and the aggregate CKA–accuracy analysis directly measure representation similarity.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures incomplete representational alignment and argues that equivalent geometric readout need not imply representational convergence. This bears on V7's partial-alignment component, but does not test convergence with scale or establish its causes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' interpretation: equivalent geometric-probe performance can coexist with representational dissimilarity, which they describe as functional convergence and a weak form of the Platonic hypothesis. Their correlation result establishes no detectable association, not independence or a failure of scale-dependent convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses reduced-rank regression for geometric readout and linear CKA for feature similarity, rather than testing scale-dependent convergence of pairwise input-distance geometries.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe rankings vary by task: the FreiHAND equivalence cluster dissolves on BIWI, and rankings differ on MPIIFaceGaze. The paper also reports layer-dependent probe accuracy and pooling-dependent results, but these are not measurements of representational similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: Five encoders achieve equivalent FreiHAND geometric-probe accuracy, including a pair with CKA 0.412.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different representations can support equivalent accuracy on separately fitted, low-dimensional linear readouts.

fits_no_version.finding: CKA and absolute probe-accuracy differences show no detectable association: Spearman rho 0.03, p 0.88.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational similarity need not predict differences in geometric-probe accuracy in this eight-model sample; the null result does not establish independence.

record.problems: The CKA analysis includes eight models and 28 non-independent pairwise comparisons; the authors say its minimum detectable correlation at 80% power is approximately 0.50, so moderate correlations could go undetected. They also note CKA reliability concerns. Representation similarity is measured on FreiHAND only, and there is no scale sweep. Probe hyperparameters are selected on the test set, although nested cross-validation is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Probe-accuracy results beyond the FreiHAND top-five group and task-specific results in Sections 4.3–4.5 and Appendices B–O are not extracted as convergence rows because they do not measure representational similarity. The paper’s patch-ablation results likewise measure task-specific probe effects, not model-to-model alignment.

untested.parts: Whether alignment increases with model size or capability. Base/large probe comparisons are not an alignment scaling test.
Alignment of paired image and caption representations as vision and language models improve.
Same-architecture networks trained from different initializations and their shared features or subspaces.
Cross-model representation mapping, stitching, relative representations, and transfer without paired data. Refitting task probes does not test these.
Recurrence of identifiable features or circuits across models. Shared target predictability does not identify shared features.
Dependence of measured alignment on similarity metrics, settings, layers, or input distributions. Probe sensitivity and cited CKA concerns do not test this version.

Whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete as training or scale increases; whether shared data or objectives explain alignment rather than a common model of reality. Training-objective ablations measure probe accuracy, not alignment causes.

record.verdict_notes: All CKA numbers match Table 12. CKA is not a percentage of shared features, and no numerical cutoff for complete convergence is supplied. The strongest V7 evidence is the explicitly discussed low-CKA pair. Higher same-family similarities do not independently establish or refute V7. Alignment was measured on one dataset using one metric at probe-selected layers.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep tests whether representation alignment rises as models get larger or more capable.
No alignment measurement on paired images and captions as vision and language models improve.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations or of their shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No test for recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.

The study does not compare similarity metrics or their settings, or measure representation similarity across different input distributions. It reports task-dependent probe performance, which is not itself a measure of representational convergence.

The study measures CKA similarity for a finite set of encoders, but does not establish whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause the measured similarities.

rows.subject: Eight-model aggregate (28 pairwise comparisons)
rows.size_stated: Six ViT-L models plus DINOv2-B and SigLIP-B
rows.operation_detail: Association between linear CKA similarity and absolute probe-accuracy difference
rows.note: The authors report no detectable correlation; the result relates representation similarity to probe-accuracy difference, not to a scale trend.
rows.check: The correlation measures whether alignment predicts probe-accuracy differences, not alignment's completeness, scaling, plateau, or causes. Retain as contextual evidence rather than a V7 result. The 28 pairs are non-independent and the null result is underpowered for moderate associations.

relationships.condition: Cross-family frozen vision encoders at their best probe layers on 8,000 FreiHAND images
relationships.reason: cka10 reports CKA 0.412 for SigLIP 2–CLIP, explicitly interpreted as representational dissimilarity despite equivalent readout; the other listed pairs also show incomplete CKA alignment. This supports only V7's incompleteness component.
relationships.display_finding: SigLIP 2 and CLIP had CKA of 0.412 despite equivalent readout, and the other encoder pairs also aligned incompletely.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
